protocol.caps: max_output_tokens=4096, outline 8192, calls 1+4U, 2M/150k tokens per song
protocol.arms: B = workflow; S4 = workflow + per-block motif quota (decode-level enum) + harness-derived acoustic guidance

objective_alignment.metric: Spearman(1 s event-start rate, librosa onset strength) from raw audio

supported: completion under identical budget: 11/11 versus 6/11 (baseline failures: 3 outline truncations, 2 provider/structural failures)
cost of that completion: +19% calls and +16% input tokens (27.2 vs 22.8 calls; 297k vs 255k tokens)
content quality on 6 fresh held-out songs: +5.58 (8B) and +3.83 (30B), both 6-0 with CIs above zero
not_supported: the earlier split-level claims (dev/test) remain unstable; only the pooled and extension results are reportable
outstanding: human review with motif ids hidden, otherwise the label confound is unavoidable
formal scale (>=12 songs) with source/artist grouping
second judge family (no local audio model qualified)

motif_label_control.note: Same plans, motif ids hidden from both versions. Judges see presentation, not only content.

time_unit_bug.description: review bundles labelled sample indices as milliseconds; event durations were 16x too long
time_unit_bug.second_defect: position swap condition never triggered, so positions were not randomised
time_unit_bug.fixed_in: report_multi.py (_actions divides by sample_rate; swap = counter % 2)

style_prior.comparison: S4 (music_structured + acoustic guidance) vs S4 + MuQ-JEV style prior

null_pairs.rule: action text identical in both arms
null_pairs.note: identical content must score zero; the judge returns exactly 0.0 on all three

changed_pairs.note: only where the prior changed the text does the judge differ; 3/3 positive but 1/3 order-inconsistent

style_prior.verdict: The field is usable and auditable, changes behaviour on half the songs, and helps only where it changes text; the effect is small.

final_dev_method.method: music_structured + deterministic acoustic guidance + vocabulary-preserving repeat rewriting (<=5 groups, 1 call each)
final_dev_method.author_check: fma-1881: D3 opens with 8 distinct sentences over 80 s; baseline repeats one sentence for 30 s
caveats: four genuine dev songs (+2 test-split songs used exploratively)
final_dev_method.verdict: First configuration with a significant content-quality gain over the workflow baseline under hidden labels (+3.9, CI [3.0,5.1], 6-0).

truncation_audit.problem: judge action text was truncated at 160 chars; baseline actions average 354 chars vs 193 for the rewritten arm, so the baseline lost more information
truncation_audit.fixed_by: re-judge at 400 chars (no truncation of either arm)
truncation_audit.split_disclosure: fma-10811 and fma-12099 belong to the test split; the six-song result therefore mixes dev and test
truncation_audit.retracted: earlier +3.92 (6 songs) and +4.5 (dev-only) were measured with 160-character truncation
truncation_audit.verdict: With fair presentation the repeat-rewriting gain is +2.2 to +3.3 points; it is not significant on the four genuine dev songs, and D and D3 are indistinguishable.

variables_ablation.note: D = free rewrite of exact duplicates; D3 = vocabulary-preserving rewrite; D4 = near-duplicate clustering with near-duplicate rejection (accepts fewer rewrites, so the metric improves less)

stable_conclusion: objective: repeat rewriting lowers verbatim repetition (baseline 0.68; D 0.37; D3/D4 0.50-0.53 with stricter guards) and never harms completion
judged: direction is positive in every arm, but on the four genuine dev songs the 95% CI crosses zero (+2.75 [-0.38,4.5]); no significant content-quality advantage is established
mechanism: judged deltas do not correlate with unique-action count, duplicate rate or action length (r ~ 0), so the judged gain cannot be attributed to the dedupe mechanism at this sample size
stricter variation guards trade metric improvement for acceptance (D4 rewrote nothing on fma-12099), because the outer model at temperature 0 cannot reliably produce genuinely different wording
